solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Freight reduced outside Lima for religious movement

indicators.note: 'outside' places one piece around another, so the word for reduced wraps round the L

blocks.note: goods carried by ship or plane
Lima is L in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A shipping firm's shrunken consignment is somehow linked to a new faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the Peruvian capital, where the freight might be headed, but here it is only the radio code word for L.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names Melanesian movements expecting Western goods to arrive through ritual, and is now used loosely of any devoted following.

clue.text: Arrive to collect luxury car for trading

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so the word for arrive takes the car inside itself

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to pick up a smart car they are trading in.
explanation.walkthrough: MERC is the everyday British short form of Mercedes, the classic luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the whole business of buying and selling goods.

clue.text: Manage to flee

blocks.note: manage, as a business or a shop

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in getting away.
explanation.walkthrough: "Manage to" reads as one phrase meaning succeed in; split it and both words define RUN, joined by "to".
explanation.definitionFit: Both are everyday senses of one verb: you can be in charge of a shop with it and bolt from a fire with it.

clue.text: Window, circular shape, that is held in both hands briefly

indicators.note: something held in the hands sits between them, so the abbreviation for that is sits between R and L

blocks.note: R and L, short for right and left

explanation.surface: Someone carries a round window pane with both hands.
explanation.walkthrough: "Both hands" are the right and the left, shortened to R and L; "briefly" signals the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular kind of window: a bay projecting from an upper storey, supported on brackets.

clue.text: Informal agreement from sitting for too long, presumably

blocks.note: the surface reading: someone has been in a chair far too long
the setter's reading: such a person has not been on their feet enough, so split the answer into a prefix meaning too little plus a word for being upright

explanation.surface: Someone claims a casual deal came about from sitting around too long.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as UNDER STANDING: someone who sits too long has done too little standing. "Presumably" flags the whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an unwritten arrangement between parties, as in 'we have an understanding'.

clue.text: Collapsed coalpit is in the news

indicators.note: a collapsed structure has fallen into a heap, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mine has fallen in and the story is making headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: The collapse sounds like the news story itself; it is the instruction to rearrange COALPIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dealing with current affairs, of interest right now.

clue.text: Escape from insect

explanation.surface: Someone is getting away from a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: "From" only links the two definitions; the surface makes it sound like the escape is away from the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both: the verb for fleeing fast and the name of the buzzing housefly.

clue.text: Try to enter stronghold with number left behind

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so the word for try goes inside the stronghold
'with' means accompanied by, so the number comes along at the end

blocks.note: have a go = have a try

explanation.surface: Soldiers attempt to storm a castle, leaving some of their number behind.
explanation.walkthrough: "Number" here is simply a specific number, TEN, not a count of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle for past participle: an umbrella forgotten on the train was left behind.

clue.text: Toy — minus its head, twice tipped over

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, so TOY loses T
twice means the remaining pair of letters is written out two times
something tipped over is upended, so in a down entry the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the definition word itself, headless and doubled

explanation.surface: A child's plaything has lost its top and been knocked over twice.
explanation.walkthrough: "Toy" does double duty: it is the definition and also the word whose letters are used: OY, then OYOY, then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the spool on a string that climbs and drops is a classic toy.

clue.text: All of us staff helpful

blocks.note: to staff a desk is to man it

explanation.surface: Every one of our employees is obliging.
explanation.walkthrough: "Staff" reads as a noun (employees) but works as the verb MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful paraphrase: the human race is everyone, all of us.

clue.text: Gathering to celebrate, not all year

blocks.note: a portion is not the whole

explanation.surface: An event for festivities that runs only part of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: "Not all year" looks like an instruction to cut YEAR short; it is PART plus Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a social occasion held to mark something.

clue.text: Gradually manoeuvre large frame

explanation.surface: Instructions to inch a big frame carefully into position.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction about a large frame; "large" is only L and "frame" alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the wooden stand that holds an artist's canvas is a frame.

clue.text: General feeling as tension is released

indicators.note: letters released from their order are free to fall into a new one

explanation.surface: A widespread mood as stress finally eases.
explanation.walkthrough: "General" suggests an army officer, but "General feeling" is the definition: a feeling that runs through a whole crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a bodily feeling and a wave of public excitement, which is what 'general' points at.

clue.text: Nuclear plant lacking a priest

indicators.note: to lack something is to be without it, so the A is removed

blocks.note: the core of a nuclear power station

explanation.surface: A nuclear station is short of a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a staffing problem at a power station; "a" is the letter to remove, not an article.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in the Church of England this is the priest in charge of a parish.

clue.text: Sort of guess one’s like this after school?

blocks.note: a guess made with some knowledge behind it
what schooling is supposed to make you

explanation.surface: A musing on what kind of guess a school leaver might make.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second definition is a playful description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: One word fits both: the idiom for an informed guess, and the state schooling leaves you in.

clue.text: Applauded, having trained a reluctant dog

indicators.note: to train something is to bend it into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An owner is praised for training a stubborn dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole 13-letter answer comes from the three words at the end; the dog-training story hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to praise someone publicly for an achievement.

clue.text: With bread, soak up seafood

explanation.surface: Advice to use bread to wipe up the juices from a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, common in Britain and northern Europe; the surface's bread and mopping belong to the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a pickled herring is a kind of seafood.

clue.text: Fine sort of key dropped

explanation.surface: A decent kind of key has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: An Allen key is the L-shaped hexagonal wrench used in flat-pack furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle for past participle: prices that have dropped have come down.

clue.text: Awful pain, caught in flap

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so its letters are in a mess

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a car door is in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: "Flap" suggests a door or pocket, but it is the informal British word for a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: to be in a flap is to be agitated and flustered.

clue.text: Adhesive tapes coming unstuck

indicators.note: to come unstuck is to fall apart, so the letters separate and reassemble

explanation.surface: Sticky tape that has stopped sticking.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is apt: tapes coming unstuck is exactly the failure an adhesive should prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a soft glue made from flour and water is an adhesive.

clue.text: Quarrel: it turns very loud

indicators.note: to turn is to face the other way, so the two letters swap direction

explanation.surface: A row that escalates into shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: FF is the musical marking fortissimo; the colon makes "it turns very loud" read as the row getting heated.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though softer: a petty squabble between friends.

clue.text: Fool almost married in characteristic style

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the word stops one letter short

explanation.surface: A near-fool gets married in a distinctive way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end: not a phrase but a style, as in a composer writing in the jazz idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The less common sense: a distinctive manner of expression in art or music.

clue.text: Second cousins tantalised nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the phrase holds the answer inside it

blocks.note: the last three letters of the first word and the first four of the second

explanation.surface: Distant relatives tease some nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: "Nurses" looks like the hospital staff being teased; it is the verb, meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun for noun: a moment so short it barely registers.

clue.text: Assistance said not to have succeeded

indicators.note: not to have something is to go without it, so the S is removed

blocks.note: s. = succeeded, as in lists of monarchs

explanation.surface: Help was offered, but reportedly it failed.
explanation.walkthrough: "Said" hints at a sound-alike, but it is the plain word SAID; the S that goes is the abbreviation for succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: help given, as in foreign aid.

clue.text: Aficionado of quiche losing pounds

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so the L goes

explanation.surface: A quiche lover goes on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a dieter; the weight lost is only the L, the sign for pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a devoted enthusiast of something.

clue.text: Obstinate swine with such personalised notepaper

blocks.note: notepaper printed with your name and address at the top

explanation.surface: A stubborn pig has its own printed stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: "With such" makes the phrase describe the answer's second half: notepaper printed with your name is headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for adjective: stubborn to the point of stupidity.
